message.reasoning:
I am responding to a trade offer in Monopoly.

I have $862 and no monopolies. I am weighing a $240 offer for my Short Line railroad.

The offer is $40 above Short Line's $200 purchase price. I would lose my only railroad and the chance to complete a set if I land on Reading. p2 would gain two railroads and higher rent.

The $40 profit is too small to justify giving up a trade asset. Strengthening p2 with an extra railroad is not worth the $240. My cash position is already healthy.

I will reject the offer. I am considering a counter-trade for more cash or a different property.

I considered trading Pacific Avenue for Short Line. That would leave me with an incomplete green set and would not help complete a monopoly.

I will reject the offer. I may raise my counter-offer to extract more value.

A $400 counter-offer would still let p2 complete a railroad set. I am now considering $450 to better reflect the value of blocking that path.

I will reject the offer outright. I do not want to raise my counter-offer to $450, as that could end negotiation or signal weakness. I will keep Short Line and let p2 know that $240 is too low for a second railroad.

A $400 counter-offer would give p2 a second railroad and double their rent. I would gain $400 cash, but lose the chance to complete a set if I land on Reading.
